A1.justification: Both 28-page PDFs contain the same complete paper, including Appendices A.1–A.5. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish that only the arXiv version/date identification differs; no material gaps limit comparison.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original activation-steering experiments across five models, including a 3.8% ESR rate for Llama-3.3-70B in Figure 2, plus original ablations, controls, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the same original empirical results, including cross-model experiments, fine-tuning outcomes, and the controls and activation analyses in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The SAE steering, contrastive latent identification, meta-prompting, and masked LoRA fine-tuning procedures are identical in Sections 2–3 and the technical appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 38 instructional prompts, 20 held-out prompts, Wikipedia-derived steering topics, and synthetic fine-tuning data. No task or domain coverage changes.

E2.justification: The five-model comparisons and comparator membership within the no-steering, latent-ablation, prefilling, and matched-prefix experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: Model and layer choices, evaluation judges and metrics, threshold calibration, trial counts, prefix lengths, and fine-tuning settings match throughout the main text and appendices.

E4.justification: Both retain identical boost sweeps, judge validation, targeted and random ablations, held-out tests, prefilling and matched-prefix controls, and sequential activation analyses.

E5.justification: Confidence intervals, significance tests, Cohen's d statistics, and the three independent random-ablation sets disclosed in Appendix A.3.4 are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including 3.8% baseline ESR in Figure 2, 2.8% ESR after targeted ablation in Figure 5, and continuation scores of 8.7, 30.4, and 54.5 in Table 6.

T1.justification: The steering and ablation equations and threshold definition in Appendix A.1 are identical. No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain identical claims about explicit ESR, detection versus sustained resistance, latent contributions, deliberate enhancement, and dual safety implications.

C2.justification: The two-component interpretation, alternative explanations, fine-tuning qualifications, and limitations concerning metrics, models, steering paradigms, and circuit identification remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, repetition penalty, judge prompts, latent-selection procedures, LoRA hyperparameters in Table 7, and the code-access statement are identical.

R1.justification: Section 4 and the reference list are unchanged, including positioning relative to activation steering, the Hydra Effect, reasoning-model self-correction, and introspection research.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv:2602.06941v2 dated 4 Jun 2026 to arXiv:2602.06941v3 dated 5 Jul 2026. This is a minor identifier/date edit; prose, terminology, authorship, and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: All 23 figures, seven tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged. Pages 2–28 render identically; page 1 differs only in the marginal version/date stamp, with the article layout preserved.

improvement.justification: The later PDF updates only arXiv version/date identification. The scientific text, experimental evidence, interpretations, limitations, reproducibility information, and appendix displays remain identical, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
